title: Uniform and Bridge
premise: In the winter of 1893, Sebastian Joubert tends the lighthouse at Cape Verren while the fiercest storms in a generation batter the coast. A sealed letter, delivered by a dying stranger washed ashore, reveals that Sebastian's late wife's family was entangled in a smuggling ring—and that a shipwrecked fortune, and a warrant, now point to his doorstep. As magistrates close in and the sea claims more ships, Sebastian must shelter the scattered remnants of that family: a fugitive brother-in-law, a niece who doesn't know her own name's weight, and an old rival who knows too much. When only one berth remains on the last boat out before the harbor freezes, Sebastian must decide who escapes and who stays to face the law—choosing at last to stop hiding behind his uniform and become the bridge between his wife's buried past and whatever future survives. In the end he gives the berth to the girl, surrenders himself as keeper of both light and secret, and finds that the family he thought he'd lost has chosen him back.
about_author: Oscar Almeida is the pen name of a former merchant marine radio operator who spent a decade collecting coastal oral histories along the Atlantic seaboard. His fiction is known for salt-weathered prose and characters who mistake duty for silence until it costs them everything.

chapters.title: The Wick and the Widow
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Establishes his routine tending Cape Verren light, his grief for wife Marguerite, and his deliberate invisibility from town gossip. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as discipline.

chapters.title: What the Sea Returned
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. During the first great storm he pulls a half-drowned stranger from the surf; the man presses a sealed letter into Sebastian's hands before losing consciousness. Beat: dread arriving wrapped in obligation.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Handwriting
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, flashback woven through present. He recognizes the letter's seal as his late wife's family crest and cannot bring himself to open it. Beat: grief reopening like a wound.

chapters.title: The Stranger in the Storeroom
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: the stranger, Tomas, wakes and bargains—he'll explain everything if Sebastian hides him from the magistrate's men already riding the coast road. Beat: complicity begins.

chapters.title: A Name He Buried
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. He opens the letter: Marguerite's family ran the wrecking ring, and a ledger naming survivors is hidden at the family house. Beat: betrayal of the dead, or of the memory of them.

chapters.title: The Girl at the Gate
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A sixteen-year-old girl, Colette, arrives claiming to be Marguerite's niece, fleeing men who searched her grandmother's house. Beat: found family knocking before he can refuse it.

chapters.title: Magistrate Perrin Comes Calling
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The magistrate inspects the lighthouse; Sebastian lies smoothly for the first time in his life while Tomas hides beneath the lamp room floor. Beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: Ledger and Ash
chapters.summary: Colette's POV. She and Sebastian ride to the ruined family house and find the ledger's hiding place emptied—burned pages, one scrap surviving with three names. Beat: hope shrinking to a single thread.

chapters.title: The Third Name
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The surviving name belongs to Aldous Renard, Marguerite's old suitor and now harbormaster—the man who could forge papers or hang them all. Beat: old rivalry resurfacing as necessity.

chapters.title: Bargaining with Renard
chapters.summary: Renard's POV. In a smoke-filled harbor office, Renard agrees to help—for the ledger's power over him erased, and a favor unnamed. Beat: uneasy alliance, everyone holding knives politely.

chapters.title: The Second Storm
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV chapters braided. The great storm strikes; Sebastian keeps the light burning through the night while Colette and Tomas shelter ships' crews in the tower. Beat: the lighthouse becomes sanctuary, not hiding place.

chapters.title: Wreck of the Meridian Star
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. A ship breaks on the shoals; in rescuing survivors, Tomas is recognized by a sailor from the old ring. Beat: the past refusing to stay drowned.

chapters.title: Testimony in the Boathouse
chapters.summary: Colette's POV. The sailor blackmails Tomas; Colette overhears and learns her family's full history—including that her father died covering their escape. Beat: inheritance redefined as burden and love at once.

chapters.title: Perrin's Net Tightens
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Warrants are issued; Renard warns them the harbor closes within the week when ice locks the channel. One fishing boat, one berth left after provisions. Beat: countdown begins.

chapters.title: What Each of Them Would Give
chapters.summary: Braided POVs. Quietly, each character offers to be the one left behind—Tomas to take blame, Colette to stay with Sebastian, even Renard hints at sacrifice. Beat: love expressed as arithmetic of loss.

chapters.title: The Sailor's Price
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The blackmailer demands the ledger scrap; Tomas steals it from Sebastian rather than let anyone be sold. Beat: protection curdling into betrayal.

chapters.title: Confrontation at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian catches Tomas at the exchange; the blackmailer is revealed as Perrin's informant all along. Standoff on the exposed flats as the tide turns. Beat: climax of trust broken and remade.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. With Perrin hours away, Sebastian chooses: Colette takes the berth, carrying the truth forward where she can live unburdened. Beat: the choice the blurb promised, made with terrible clarity.

chapters.title: Uniform
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. He puts on his keeper's coat and walks to meet Perrin, confessing everything but surrendering nothing of the others. Beat: invisibility abandoned; accountability embraced.

chapters.title: Bridge
chapters.summary: Renard's POV. Renard uses his harbormaster's authority to stall Perrin's men as the boat slips the freezing channel—an unnamed favor repaid. Beat: rival becomes kin.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. At trial, testimony from storm survivors and Colette's letter from abroad reframes him as rescuer, not conspirator; Perrin, exposed by the informant scandal, withdraws. Beat: justice imperfect but merciful.

chapters.title: Light Over Frozen Water
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, spring. Colette returns; Tomas sends word from a new life overseas; Renard shares a quiet drink in the lamp room. The family, chosen and tested, gathers under the light. Beat: resolution—inheritance transformed into belonging.
